column5: regmove will not tie an AND to a parameter copy unless the next insn sets it again: mask and shift the parameter in place (flags &= m; flags >>= 12), then a separate priority = flags - 1.
A chain of early returns (if (!p) return 0; ...) with one object = input copy read only by the last test keeps both pointer registers; nested ifs and && chains let cse merge them.
The graphic index is narrowed in the call: (u16)(entry->graphic + 0x121); the truncation that combine later proves redundant keeps the constant load and copy apart from the byte.

A plain for loop that indexes a parts base pointer declared in the body (parts[i]) plus an inline SetAction(state, 1, 5) helper gives the hoisted constants and giv order; the hand-rotated pointer walk needed the pin.

Same indexed for loop; the queue-part step is an inline helper whose body is the shared ARMOR_QUEUE_PART_ACTION statement macro, which doubles the count pointer refs (the r3/r4 order) and leaves the dead zero pseudo that owns r8.

cse (fold_rtx) always moves a register with a known constant second, so the ROM order base+offset needs the base set outside the add's cse block (cse stops at a NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END, i.e. a statement macro around the base setup); no shared macro is evident for it.
A two-case switch written case 23 then case 10 gives the ROM's layout, and a second manager view pointer read only in the case 10 arm (reached through a label) keeps the early r1-to-r3 copy.
Two plain for loops over one index; the byte is updated in place with two compound assignments (buffer[i] ^= word; buffer[i] &= mask), which loop.c turns into the pointer walk and countdown itself.
Plain field code: p->flags88 |= 2; p->flags88 &= ~1; as two statements (README fact 103) gives the or-with-zero, and the literal 1 is shared by cse; no named constants needed.
Field code with no locals: if (++particle->frame > 15), offsetY += velocityY, and the phase test read from particle->frame again; cse supplies the registers the pins forced.

ROM keeps p in r4 for the inlined hit test and a top-of-function copy in r5 for the tail; cse makes the copy the class head and deletes p in every ordinary form tried (copy, inline, early returns, goto).
One slot variable carries the next window, then its previous-link address, then the window's own previous slot after the join; with separate variables the allocator puts next in r1.

Without the r0 pin the sample and the coordinate swap r0/r2: local-alloc ranks the coordinate quantity (12 refs) above the sample (8 refs) in every ordinary form tried (types, operand order, shared or per-block variables).
